contract: AIDEFEND framework edition and semantic migration registry

sourceArtifact.publicationDateStatus: not set in the v1.0 PDF

sourceLicense.attribution: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026, OWASP Foundation / OWASP GenAI Security Project
sourceLicense.scope: OWASP-derived identifiers, names, edition metadata, and normalized risk summaries
sourceLicense.changesMade: Risk summaries are paraphrased and normalized for the AIDEFEND catalog; presentation is reformatted; AIDEFEND mapping decisions, migration analysis, and resolver behavior are independently authored.

resolutionPolicy.explicitSupersededId: resolve by the declared semantic successor, never by same-rank number
resolutionPolicy.legacyName: resolve by the named risk concept and return its current successor
resolutionPolicy.bareId: treat the rank as belonging to the current edition
resolutionPolicy.nonPaddedRank: normalize LLM1 through LLM9 to the canonical two-digit rank before resolution
resolutionPolicy.editionContext: treat an edition in a recognized OWASP LLM label, or an adjacent OWASP year context, as explicit for an otherwise bare LLM rank
resolutionPolicy.malformedOrUnsupportedEdition: return structured invalid metadata; never reinterpret it as a current bare rank
resolutionPolicy.multipleConcepts: return structured ambiguity with current canonical candidates; never choose by catalog order
resolutionPolicy.unversionedIdNameConflict: a recognized current or legacy risk name identifies the concept; return the current successor and report normalization
resolutionPolicy.versionedIdNameConflict: a recognized risk name identifies the concept even when a versioned rank conflicts; return the named concept's current successor and report normalization
resolutionPolicy.mappingCarryForward: never automatic; AIDEFEND mappings require target-edition semantic review

activeItems.name: Prompt Injection
activeItems.description: Untrusted or unintended content in any modality or context source changes model behavior, including content delivered through retrieval, tool output, persistent memory, images, audio, or video.

activeItems.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
activeItems.description: Confidential, regulated, privileged, or proprietary data is exposed through answers, tool arguments, reasoning traces, retrieved chunks, logs, embeddings, multimodal output, or inference side channels.

activeItems.name: Excessive Agency
activeItems.description: Unexpected or manipulated model output causes damaging action because an application grants excessive tool functionality, permissions, or autonomy.

activeItems.name: Supply Chain
activeItems.description: Compromise, substitution, vulnerability, or ungoverned trust in third-party data, models, adapters, packages, transformation pipelines, deployment platforms, or on-device artifacts undermines the LLM application.

activeItems.name: Data and Model Poisoning
activeItems.description: Manipulated data or model artifacts create durable harmful behavior, bias, backdoors, or exploitable weaknesses during training, fine-tuning, retrieval, feedback, persistent memory, or model transformation.

activeItems.name: Unbounded Consumption
activeItems.description: Missing resource controls permit excessive inference, token, reasoning, multimodal, session, queue, tool, or infrastructure consumption that harms availability, creates unsustainable cost, or enables model cloning.

activeItems.name: Misinformation
activeItems.description: Incorrect, incomplete, unsupported, or misleading model output appears credible enough to drive a harmful human decision, workflow, or agent action.

activeItems.name: Hidden Context Exposure
activeItems.description: Hidden instructions or operational context are extracted, inferred, or reconstructed in a way that reveals secrets, policy logic, tool schemas, trust boundaries, or other details that materially increase attacker capability.

activeItems.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
activeItems.description: Embedding geometry or similarity-search mechanics enable cross-tenant inference, inversion, retrieval poisoning or jamming, membership inference, semantic-cache poisoning, or multimodal retrieval manipulation.

activeItems.name: Improper Output Handling
activeItems.description: Model output is insufficiently validated, sanitized, encoded, or constrained before a downstream component interprets, renders, executes, stores, or transmits it.

migrations.note: The 2026 risk explicitly adds cross-modal delivery, tool output, persistent memory, cross-session propagation, and trusted-backend surfaces.
The 2026 risk explicitly includes tool arguments, reasoning traces, embeddings, telemetry, derived artifacts, and observable inference side channels.
The risk moved from rank 3 to rank 4 and now explicitly treats promoted artifacts, adapters, conversion, merge, quantization, and on-device delivery as first-class supply-chain surfaces.
The risk moved from rank 4 to rank 5 and more explicitly covers fine-tuning subversion, feedback loops, persistent memory, and inference artifacts.
The risk moved from rank 5 to rank 10 and now explicitly includes unsafe generated code, terminal/control-character sinks, and automatic outbound rendering.
The risk moved from rank 6 to rank 3 and clarifies excessive functionality, permissions, autonomy, user-context preservation, complete mediation, and damage-limiting controls.

The successor is broader than system-prompt leakage. It covers extraction, inference, or reconstruction of model-visible hidden operational context and assumes that context is discoverable; it does not imply that every former mapping remains valid.

The risk moved from rank 8 to rank 9 and now requires an embedding-geometry or similarity-search mechanism, while expanding treatment of inversion, jamming, membership inference, caches, and multimodal embeddings.
The risk moved from rank 9 to rank 7 and emphasizes incorrect, incomplete, unsupported, or misleading output that is trusted and acted upon.
The risk moved from rank 10 to rank 6 and now explicitly includes thinking-token exhaustion, multimodal cost, agent/tool fan-out, hard spending caps, and model cloning through resource abuse.
